name: Earn the Trust of Others
definition: Leaders are sincerely open-minded, genuinely listen, and examine their own strongest convictions with humility. They value diversity in all its forms because different viewpoints result in novel ideas.

rows.under: Waits for their turn to talk. The other person can tell they were not heard.
rows.justRight: Listens all the way through, and changes the plan when they are right.
rows.over: Agrees with everyone so nobody is upset, and the decision is mush.

rows.situation: When a fact challenges a view you hold strongly
rows.under: Defends the view because it is yours.
rows.justRight: Examines the conviction with humility. Keeps it only if it still holds.
rows.over: Abandons a sound view at the first challenge so they can look open-minded.

rows.situation: When the room is of one mind
rows.under: Treats that as proof the idea is right.
rows.justRight: Seeks a viewpoint the room does not already have, because novel ideas come from that friction.
rows.over: Collects viewpoints as a ritual and never lets them change the work.

rows.situation: When you still have to decide
rows.under: Closes the question before anyone else has been heard.
rows.justRight: Stays open long enough to learn, then takes a position people can trust.
rows.over: Stays so open that nobody can tell what you believe, and trust erodes.

rows.situation: When people are deciding whether to bring you the real news
rows.under: Punishes the messenger. The next miss arrives late.
rows.justRight: Makes it safe to bring a hard fact, including one that contradicts you. That is how trust is earned.
rows.over: Asks for candor, then uses the note against the person later.
